Query Elasticsearch as the signed-in user

Source: R/backend__elasticsearch.R
oauth_db_elasticsearch_api.Rd

Search documents, run SQL or use ES|QL with each visitor's access token. Results keep Elasticsearch's native JSON structure as R lists.

Usage

oauth_db_elasticsearch_api(
  authorization,
  url,
  client_secret = NULL,
  target = NULL,
  required_scopes = character(),
  min_valid_for = 60,
  timeout = 30,
  ca_bundle = NULL,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

Function providing the visitor's current sign-in authorization. Pass auth$connection from shinyOAuth without parentheses. To select a saved account, use a function calling auth$connection(id).

url

HTTPS Elasticsearch deployment URL, including a proxy path if needed.

client_secret

JWT realm's application shared secret. This is separate from the OAuth registration's client secret. Use NULL only when the realm explicitly disables client authentication.

target

Name of the service token to use in your shinyOAuth client. Named targets let one sign-in obtain tokens for different services. NULL uses the client's default token.

required_scopes

Additional OAuth permissions to check before use. Request them on the shinyOAuth client first; this check doesn't request consent or grant database privileges.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

timeout

Maximum seconds for one HTTP operation, including a read retry.

ca_bundle

Optional path to a trusted CA certificate bundle.

session

The visitor's Shiny session. Usually inferred when you create the helper inside server().

Value

A client object with these methods:

  • $search(index = NULL, body = list(), query = list(), raw = FALSE) runs a JSON search. The index may be a name, pattern or character vector; NULL searches across the deployment.

  • $sql(sql, parameters = list(), raw = FALSE) returns one SQL result page, including columns, rows and any cursor.

  • $esql(query, parameters = list(), raw = FALSE) returns ES|QL columns, values and completion metadata.

  • $request(path, method = "GET", query = list(), body = NULL, raw = FALSE) calls a JSON API using relative path segments.

Details

Configure an Elasticsearch JWT realm to accept the provider's JWT access tokens and map their principal and groups to Elasticsearch roles. The access_token realm type requires allowed subjects or subject patterns. JWT realms require Elasticsearch 8.7 or later for this token type and an appropriate subscription. This route supports self-managed and Elastic Cloud Hosted deployments; Elastic Cloud Serverless has no JWT realms. Kibana OIDC sign-in alone does not configure API access.

Create the client inside server(). Each request obtains a current access token and discards results after sign-out, account changes or lost required permissions. GET and HEAD can refresh and retry once after HTTP 401. POST queries and writes are never replayed automatically. Requests use verified HTTPS and do not follow redirects.

The realm shared secret identifies the application; the visitor's token determines their data permissions. It is sent in the redacted ES-Client-Authentication header. No ID token, API key or impersonation header is substituted for the visitor's access token.

Parameters and results

SQL and ES|QL accept ? placeholders with an unnamed list of scalar strings, logicals, finite numbers or NULL in parameters. Values are sent separately from the query. ES|QL and its parameter syntax require a server version that supports them. Use $request() for other native parameter forms or query options.

Large JSON integers remain strings; nested documents and multivalued fields remain lists. Search timeouts, shard failures and partial query results raise errors. Use raw = TRUE for the httr2 response instead.

There is no automatic pagination. Use search_after for searches, or $request("_sql", method = "POST", body = list(cursor = cursor)) for SQL pages. Close unused SQL cursors with $request(c("_sql", "close"), method = "POST", body = list(cursor = cursor)). Keep cursors and point-in-time identifiers with the authorization that created them and discard them on sign-out or account changes. NDJSON APIs need a different client.

See also

vignette("elasticsearch", package = "shinyOAuthDB").

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
search <- oauth_db_elasticsearch_api(auth$connection,
  url = "https://search.example.org",
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_ELASTICSEARCH_REALM_SECRET"))
output$rows <- shiny::renderPrint({
  search$sql("SELECT country, total FROM orders WHERE country = ?",
    parameters = list("NL"))$rows
})
} # }
